method: keywords-explorer-matching-terms, match_mode=terms, one broad sightseeing phrase per language, ordered by volume, with a per-language volume floor chosen so the response stays about 100 rows. The phrase is the one that language actually uses, not a translation of the English one: sehenswurdigkeiten, que faire a, cosa vedere, que ver en, bezienswaardigheden, atrakcje, o que fazer em. Raw rows are in harvest-2026-10-01.csv.
why: The localisation gate rejects 46,120 rows as LOCAL_DEMAND_NOT_FOR_THIS_DESTINATION, and it is right to, because the evidence file behind it covered roughly 333 destinations and 59 measured outbound pairs. That is a limit of the measurement, not of the demand. Asking the demand side directly, one call per language, is how to find out which rejections are true and which are the measurement being thin.

findings.noise_that_had_to_be_excluded: que ver en netflix 12,000, que ver hoy en tv 9,100, cosa vedere su netflix 9,300, cosa vedere stasera in tv 9,000, que faire a manger 1,600, atrakcje dla dzieci 6,300, energylandia atrakcje 3,900. A phrase match on a sightseeing verb catches television listings and a theme park. Every row here was classified by hand against the gazetteer rather than accepted because it matched.

what_this_does_not_say: It does not say the pages exist. A measured destination still has to pass the source, completeness, SERP, usefulness and cannibalisation gates, and a region or island page needs an entity record and real data behind it, neither of which the entity graph holds yet. The harvest is demand evidence and nothing more.
